correctness.rationale: The diagonal conjugation action preserves both spectra in the coincidence condition. A generic cocharacter has one zero-weight diagonal subspace and pairwise distinct nonzero weights on off-diagonal matrix units. Every diagonal fixed point has the cutoff spectrum as a submultiset of the full spectrum, while every off-diagonal matrix unit and its cutoff are nilpotent; therefore every ambient fixed point has maximal common multiplicity. The fixed locus on every closed level is consequently one projective space of dimension one less than the matrix size together with the off-diagonal coordinate points, whose Euler characteristic is the square of the matrix size. For every lower exact stratum the fixed locus is empty, so compactly supported Euler characteristic vanishes. The packaged checker verifies the weight separation and finite boundary cases.

value.rationale: The eigenvalue-coincidence filtration is a central geometric object in the cited papers and has nontrivial codimension and component behavior. The theorem gives a uniform global topological invariant across every closed level and a sharper vanishing theorem for every nonmaximal exact stratum. The conclusion is structurally informative: although the algebraic geometry changes with the coincidence level, the projectivized Euler characteristic does not, and all compactly supported Euler mass is forced into the deepest stratum. This is a natural invariant of the full literature-defined family, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
